title: Best Hotels in Montreal with a Pool: Where to Stay and Swim
excerpt: Swimming matters when you're traveling. Here are the best hotels in Montreal with pools that won't drain your budget, plus insider tips for maximizing your stay.
content:
## Why a Pool Matters in Montreal

Montreal summers are hot and humid, while winters are brutally cold. A good hotel pool isn't just a luxury—it's practical. Whether you're cooling off after exploring the Plateau-Mont-Royal or recovering from jet lag, a quality pool gives you a reason to stay at the hotel and relax. The best hotels in Montreal with pools balance amenities with realistic pricing, making them worth the investment.

## Top Montreal Hotels with Pools

**Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth** ($180-280 USD per night)

Located in Downtown Montreal on Boulevard René-Lévesque, this is the gold standard. The heated indoor pool sits on the 17th floor with views over the city, and it's open year-round. The hotel connects directly to the Underground City, so you never need to face winter weather. Service is impeccable, and the location puts you steps from major attractions. Book early in summer; rates spike June through August.

**Hotel le Germain Maple Leaf Square** ($140-200 USD per night)

If you prefer Old Montreal's character over downtown corporate energy, this boutique hotel delivers. The indoor pool is smaller but heated, and the neighborhood around Vieux-Montréal offers cobblestone streets, galleries, and excellent restaurants. You're close to the Old Port and the Basilica-Cathedral Marie-Reine-du-Monde. The location trades some city views for authentic atmosphere.

**Hyatt Centric Montreal Downtown** ($130-190 USD per night)

This is your middle ground. The rooftop pool opens seasonally (May through September), and while it's not heated year-round, the views of downtown justify it. The hotel sits near the Quartier des Spectacles, meaning endless dining and nightlife options. Rooms are modern, and rates are more reasonable than Fairmont without sacrificing quality.

**Le Centre Sheraton Montreal** ($120-160 USD per night)

For budget-conscious travelers who refuse to skip the pool, this is your answer. The indoor pool is solid, heated, and open year-round. Located downtown near Gare Centrale, you have easy metro access to all neighborhoods. Service is professional, and you save 30-40% compared to luxury brands while keeping essential amenities.

## Choosing the Right Neighborhood

Monitoba's geography shapes your experience. **Downtown** is central and safe, but sterile. **Old Montreal** (Vieux-Montréal) is picturesque and walkable, perfect for first-timers. The **Plateau-Mont-Royal** attracts young travelers seeking bars and vintage shops—no major hotels with pools here, but it's a 20-minute metro ride from downtown options. **Griffintown** is emerging as a trendy industrial neighborhood with restaurants and galleries; it's 10 minutes from downtown via metro.

## Local Tips That Actually Help

Book direct or through hotel websites, not OTA sites. Montreal hotels often offer loyalty rates and package deals that don't appear on aggregators. The difference is 15-20%.

Visit the **Musée des Beaux-Arts** on Wednesday evenings when entry is free. You'll cover world-class art in two hours, leaving time to return to your pool before dinner.

Montreal tap water is excellent. Fill refillable bottles and skip overpriced hotel bottled water.

The **metro system** is clean, fast, and uses single-fare cards (roughly $3 USD). Buy a 5-day pass ($25 USD) if staying that long—it saves money and eliminates decision fatigue.

Winter pools are psychological wins. Even if you don't swim, watching Montreal's frozen landscape through steam-covered windows from an indoor pool feels like victory.

## Budget Tips for Montreal

Visit May or September for shoulder season pricing. Expect 25-30% lower rates than June-August while enjoying pleasant weather.

Many downtown hotels include Underground City access. This matters in winter—you can shop and eat without stepping outside.

Weekday rates are 20-30% cheaper than weekends. If flexible, avoid Friday and Saturday nights.

Pack your own snacks. Hotel mini-bars and room service drain budgets quickly. The **Jean-Talon Market** (if staying north) or corner dépanneurs offer excellent cheese, fruit, and bread at fair prices.

## Final Thoughts

The best hotels in Montreal with pools combine location, year-round amenities, and reasonable pricing. Your budget determines whether you choose Fairmont's luxury or Le Centre Sheraton's practicality, but don't skip the pool—it's what keeps you sane during extremes and reminds you to breathe during busy sightseeing days.
